lessons.remember: Collibra, Alation and Informatica are cross-platform governance suites for formal governance programmes; their value depends on the people and processes behind them.

lessons.title: Great Expectations
lessons.summary: Great Expectations (the open-source library is now called GX Core, version 1.x since August 2024) is a Python framework for testing data.
lessons.remember: GX Core lets Python pipelines declare expectations about data, validate batches and publish readable results.

lessons.title: Soda
lessons.summary: Soda is a data quality tool where checks are written in YAML rather than code.
lessons.remember: Soda checks data with YAML definitions, and since v4 centres on data contracts verified against each dataset.

lessons.title: Deequ and PyDeequ
lessons.summary: Deequ is an open-source library from AWS Labs, written in Scala on Apache Spark, for "unit tests for data".
lessons.remember: Deequ computes and checks data quality metrics efficiently on Spark, but PyDeequ's JVM dependency limits it on modern Spark Connect platforms.

lessons.title: Data observability platforms
lessons.summary: Data observability applies monitoring ideas from software to data: instead of writing every rule by hand, a platform watches datasets continuously and alerts on anomalies.
lessons.remember: Data observability watches freshness, volume, schema, distribution and lineage automatically to catch the problems no test anticipated.

lessons.title: Data contracts
lessons.summary: A data contract is an explicit, versioned agreement between a data producer (an application team, a source system owner) and its consumers about a dataset: schema (columns, types, meaning), quality rules, freshness and a
lessons.remember: A data contract is an enforced, versioned agreement on schema, quality and ownership between producer and consumers.

lessons.title: ClickHouse
lessons.summary: ClickHouse is an open-source (Apache 2.0) column-oriented OLAP database built for very fast aggregations over large volumes of event-style data.
lessons.remember: ClickHouse is a columnar OLAP database whose sorted MergeTree tables make aggregations over billions of events fast.

lessons.title: Apache Druid and Apache Pinot
lessons.summary: Two open-source real-time OLAP stores built for low-latency queries on fresh event data, often directly from Kafka: - Apache Druid: ingests streams (Kafka, Kinesis) and batches into time-partitioned segments with indexes
lessons.remember: Druid and Pinot serve fresh event data to many concurrent users with millisecond latency; Pinot leans to user-facing analytics.

lessons.title: Power BI
lessons.summary: Power BI is Microsoft's business intelligence tool: - Power BI Desktop (free, Windows) to model data and build reports.
lessons.remember: Power BI pairs a strong semantic model engine with Microsoft's ecosystem, and inside Fabric reads OneLake directly.

lessons.title: Tableau
lessons.summary: Tableau is a visual analytics platform, part of Salesforce since 2019.
lessons.remember: Tableau is Salesforce's visual analytics platform, strongest at exploration, with Tableau Next adding semantics and AI agents.

lessons.title: Semantic layers and metrics stores
lessons.summary: A semantic layer defines business concepts (metrics such as revenue or active customers, dimensions, joins, filters) once, in one place, and exposes them to every consumer: BI tools, notebooks, applications and, increasi
lessons.remember: A semantic layer defines metrics once for every tool and for AI; it lives in the BI tool, the platform, or a universal layer.

lessons.title: Docker and containers
lessons.summary: A container packages an application with its dependencies (Python version, libraries, system packages, configuration) so it runs the same everywhere.
lessons.remember: A container image packages code with its dependencies so the tested artefact is exactly what runs.

lessons.title: Kubernetes
lessons.summary: Kubernetes orchestrates containers across a cluster of machines.
lessons.remember: Kubernetes runs and scales containers declaratively across a cluster; powerful for data services, but it needs a team to operate.

lessons.title: Terraform and infrastructure as code
lessons.summary: Infrastructure as code (IaC) describes cloud resources (storage accounts, networks, Databricks workspaces, Fabric capacities, Snowflake warehouses, permissions) in files kept in Git, and tools create or update the real r
lessons.remember: Terraform declares infrastructure in code, plans changes against stored state and applies them; keep state safe and avoid manual drift.

lessons.title: CI/CD for data platforms
lessons.summary: CI/CD automates checking and deploying changes.
lessons.remember: CI tests every change and CD promotes the same artefact through environments with approvals, using each platform's deployment tooling.

lessons.title: Secrets and identity
lessons.summary: Pipelines need to authenticate to databases, storage and APIs.
lessons.remember: Prefer managed identities and federation over stored secrets; keep unavoidable secrets in a vault and grant least privilege.

lessons.title: MLflow
lessons.summary: MLflow is the most widely used open-source platform for the ML lifecycle (Linux Foundation; version 3.x since mid-2025).
lessons.remember: MLflow records runs, packages models with signatures, registers versions with aliases, and now traces and evaluates GenAI apps.

lessons.title: Feature store products
lessons.summary: A feature store keeps ML features (customer's orders in the last 30 days, average basket size) in two forms: an offline store (warehouse or lake tables for training, with point-in-time correct joins) and an online store
lessons.remember: Feature store products manage offline features for training and online features for serving from one definition; adopt one when features are shared and served in real time.

lessons.title: Vector databases and vector search
lessons.summary: Vector search finds items whose embeddings are closest to a query embedding, the core of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search and recommendations.
lessons.remember: Vector search uses ANN indexes such as HNSW, IVF or DiskANN; start with vector features in your existing platform and add hybrid keyword search.

lessons.title: Model serving platforms
lessons.summary: Model serving puts a trained model behind an API so applications can get predictions in real time.
lessons.remember: Serve models in real time only when needed, using a managed endpoint or a Kubernetes serving framework, with vLLM-style engines for LLMs.

lessons.title: Cloud map: ingestion, streaming and storage
lessons.summary: Each cloud offers a similar set of building blocks under different names.
lessons.remember: Every cloud has object storage, a streaming service, a CDC service and a batch mover; the names differ more than the ideas.

lessons.title: Cloud map: processing and orchestration
lessons.summary: For the processing and orchestration layers: Role AWS Azure Google Cloud ------------ Managed Spark Amazon EMR (EC2, EKS, Serverless), AWS Glue Azure Databricks, Fabric Spark, Synapse Spark (earlier service) Dataproc, Se
lessons.remember: Each cloud pairs managed Spark, serverless SQL, a warehouse, stream processing and an orchestrator; Databricks and Snowflake sit across all three.

lessons.title: Cloud map: governance, BI and ML
lessons.summary: For governance, consumption and ML (names as of October 2026): Role AWS Azure / Microsoft Google Cloud ------------ Technical catalog AWS Glue Data Catalog OneLake catalog, Unity Catalog (Azure Databricks) Dataplex Unive
lessons.remember: Each cloud has a catalog, an access layer, a BI tool and an ML platform; their names change fast, so check current names before designing.
